newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Melrose sees Newco listing in Dec.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Melrose sees Newco listing in Dec.

text.p: Melrose Energy Plc said on Monday it expected Newco, the company it set up for its recent Siberian oil deal, to be listed on the Alternative Investment Market early in December.
Finance director and deputy chairman Robert Adair told Reuters that Melrose wants the listing to be completed before actively looking for further investment possibilities in Russia.
"The listing has our priority at the moment," Adair said.
Melrose earlier reported that its full-year pre-tax profit climbed 162 percent to 15.3 million stg, mainly due to the December acquisition of Pentex Oil.
The success of the fund raising in January for the Melrose IV series of limited partnerships was another major contributor to profit growth.
The limited partnerships are set up to find the money for low-risk drilling operations in the U.S.
A new series will be marketed in the first quarter of 1997 with Melrose looking to raise 20 to 25 million stg, Adair said. The last partnerships series raised 14.1 million stg.
Earlier this month Melrose announced it set up Newco, in which it will hold 49 percent, to buy an indirect 10 percent stake for 19.69 million stg in a western Siberian oil venture.
The purchase meant that the Russian assets were acquired at about $0.17 per barrel of oil, Adair said.
He expected Newco to be valued at the AIM within a price equivalent to $0.45 and $2.0 per barrel as seen for other oil firms with interests in Russia.
"We would hope to see some good uplift in the share value in the UK," Adair added.
Total recoverable reserves attributable to Newco's indirect investments are about 175 million barrels of oil.
